frameBudget.note: Cost a block against computeClocksPerFrame. videoClocksPerFrameZ60 is the scanout period and answers a different question.

rate.workloadSource: Same population as zhao_geom_skin -- this is the projector the skinned and warped vertices reach the screen through, per its own header. NOT a separately derived figure, and it is the number that makes the duplication with zhao_terrain_project expensive: 120,000 vertices at one per clock is 7.2% of the frame, so a SHARED projector is affordable and two are not justified by rate.
docs/OWNER_DOCKET.md 2026-08-23, "Where the remaining 188 multipliers sit": ~270 patches/frame, already costed against the 1.67 M budget.

docs/OWNER_DOCKET.md 2026-08-23: 10 deform events/s x 25 vertices is 4.2 normals/frame; rebuilding the entire 65,536-vertex field once per second is 1,092. 2,000 is the ruled demand, generous against both.

The 120,000 weighted vertices/frame ruling, independently corroborated in docs/OWNER_DOCKET.md 2026-08-23 across 93 retail creature models (median 2,951 vertices; a defensible scene is 40-60 skinned characters, so 40 x 2,951 = 118,040).

docs/OWNER_DOCKET.md 2026-08-23, TEXTURE.TMU demand table: Z60 384x240 at overdraw 3.0 is 829,440 samples/frame; 850,000 is the ruled figure with headroom. Terrain is CLUT8, so the CLUT path is the demand-critical one.
docs/OWNER_DOCKET.md 2026-08-23: heavy-barrage measurement is ~6,000 texels/frame; 20,000 is 3x that as the ruled demand.

limitations: No number in this file was typed. Each is copied from reports/rtl_inventory.json, reports/synthesis/zhao_block_map.json, reports/synthesis/zhao_block_fit.json or design/budgets/workloads.yml, and each row names the commit its measurement came from.
mapDspBlocks and mapEstimatedAlms come from Analysis and Synthesis. The DSP figure matched the fitter on every block cross-checked; the ALM figure is an estimate and is NOT comparable to fitAlms.
A map row carries NO timing. Every Fmax and slack in this file comes from the fit lane, at the commit named in fitCommit.

criticalPathFamily names the expensive cones the SOURCE contains. It is not an STA result -- no per-block STA report in this repo carries a path family, and naming one from the source is honest where inventing one would not be.
inferredMinII is a lower bound derived from the state graph. Where a measured II exists in workloads.yml it is used instead and the row says which.
